sections.title: Coast redwood
sections.text: This plate represents Sequoia sempervirens, the coast redwood, an evergreen conifer native to the Pacific coast of California and southern Oregon. Its straight reddish-brown trunk can exceed 100 m in height and 6 m in diameter near the base. Flattened, two-ranked foliage and small woody cones distinguish it from the giant sequoia.

sections.title: Ecology and uses
sections.text: Coast redwood is the tallest tree species; its longevity can exceed two millennia. It is widely planted as an ornamental and valued for durable timber. The cited sources describe no food use.
